# Titles are lines that are non-empty and do not start with '-' and do not contain ':' (to exclude director/genre lines)
# But there might be headings like '# Movie Recommendations' — we exclude those containing 'Movie Recommendations'

titles=[]
for line in lines:
    s=line.strip()
    if not s:
        continue
    if s.startswith('#'):
        continue
    if s.startswith('-'):
        continue
    if 'director:' in s or 'genre:' in s:
        continue
    if s.lower().startswith('movie recommendations'):
        continue
    # likely title line
    if ':' in s:
        continue
    titles.append(s)

print('num_titles', len(titles))
print('titles', titles)

# Parse Simple Note 'Movie Recommendations' to extract titles with director Quentin Tarantino
simple_pw=[x['password'] for x in apis.supervisor.show_account_passwords() if x['account_name']=='simple_note'][0]
access_token=apis.simple_note.login(username='gl.moore@gmail.com', password=simple_pw)['access_token']
note=apis.simple_note.show_note(note_id=1556, access_token=access_token)
content=note['content']
lines=content.splitlines()

movies=[]
current_title=None
for line in lines:
    s=line.strip()
    if not s:
        continue
    if s.startswith('#'):
        continue
    if s.lower().startswith('movie recommendations'):
        continue
    if s.startswith('-'):
        # director line
        if s.lower().startswith('- director:'):
            director=s.split(':',1)[1].strip()
            if current_title is not None and director.lower()=='quentin tarantino':
                movies.append(current_title)
        continue
    # title line: exclude any line that looks like metadata with ':'
    if ':' in s:
        continue
    current_title=s

# unique while preserving order
seen=set()
uniq=[]
for m in movies:
    if m not in seen:
        uniq.append(m)
        seen.add(m)

print('tarantino_movies_count', len(uniq))
print('tarantino_movies', uniq)
print('comma_separated', ', '.join(uniq))
